title: How a bird glides without flapping
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: How can a bird fly without flapping?
How do eagles soar so high?

forces.label: Weight
forces.ask: Why does a gliding bird slowly sink?

explain.say: A gliding bird is pulled down by its weight, just like anything else. To stay up without flapping, it needs a force pushing up.

draw.text: How a bird glides without flapping

forces.label: Weight
forces.ask: Why does a gliding bird slowly sink?

explain.say: Its wings are curved and held at a slight angle. As air flows past, the wing pushes air downward, and the air pushes the wing upward with a force called lift.

forces.label: Weight
forces.ask: Why does a gliding bird slowly sink?

explain.say: Air also pushes back against the bird, a force called drag. With no flapping to push it forward, a gliding bird trades a little height for speed, sliding gently down through the air like a sledge down a hill.

forces.label: Weight
forces.ask: Why does a gliding bird slowly sink?

explain.say: To glide for hours, birds like vultures and eagles ride rising air, such as warm thermals or wind pushed up by cliffs. If the air rises faster than the bird sinks, it climbs without a single flap.

forces.ask: Why does a gliding bird slowly sink?

faq.a: A wing is curved and tilted slightly upward at the front. It turns the air flowing past it downward, and pushing air down pushes the wing up. The air pressure above the wing also drops, adding to the lift.
Drag, the push of the air against its body and wings. Gliding birds have smooth, streamlined shapes to keep drag small.
asks: What is drag on a bird?

faq.q: Why does a gliding bird slowly sink?
faq.a: Without flapping, nothing pushes it forward, so it uses gravity instead, tilting slightly downhill to keep up its speed. A good glider like an albatross travels many metres forward for every metre it drops.
A thermal is a column of warm air rising from ground heated by the Sun. Birds such as vultures and storks circle inside thermals to climb high without flapping.
asks: How do eagles soar so high?

faq.q: Which bird is the best glider?
faq.a: The wandering albatross, with wings over 3 metres across, can glide for hours over the ocean using the wind above the waves, barely flapping at all.
asks: Which bird can glide the furthest?

facts: The wandering albatross has the largest wingspan of any living bird, up to about 3.5 metres.
Soaring birds such as vultures and storks use rising thermals to gain height without flapping.

quiz.say: A vulture circles higher and higher without flapping. What is lifting it?
quiz.show: A vulture climbs without flapping by…

options.show: Riding rising warm air called a thermal
options.say: Riding rising warm air called a thermal

quiz.why: In a thermal the air rises faster than the gliding bird sinks, so the bird is carried upward.

wrong.0: Weight pulls the bird down, not up.
wrong.2: Drag pushes back against the bird's motion; it doesn't lift it.
